code.label: A program, with no model call.

human.label: A person who does work: nothing runs while they do it.

wait.label: Nobody: the run waits for something outside (CI, a deployment, a date).

gate.label: A person who decides: they approve or refuse what a step produced.

judge.text: Can the person who approves really judge what they approve?

yes.label: Yes: they are shown something they can read and refuse.

no.label: No: nobody could tell a good one from a bad one.

survive.text: How long does it live, and what must survive?

restart.label: Minutes to a few hours; starting again from its beginning is acceptable.

midway.label: Days inside one computation, or it must not run twice, or every run must be replayable step by step.

spread.text: Does the work split into many independent units?

one.label: No: one unit of work, or a few parts that one writer handles.

many.label: Yes: tens or hundreds of units that do not depend on each other.

repos.text: How many repositories need this step?

one.label: One: the step lives in a file of that repository.

several.label: Several: the same step, kept the same everywhere.

determined.text: Is the right output determined by the inputs?

yes.label: Yes: the same inputs always give the same right output. The step is a program.

no.label: No: it needs interpretation. The step is an agent.

weakness.text: Is this step here because today's model is weak?

yes.label: Yes: a better model would make the step useless.

no.label: No: the step would still be needed with a better model.

code.name: Plain code
code.where: A tested command of the repository, started by a short CI job.
code.why: The right output is determined by the inputs: a program gives it every time, a prompt only most of the time.

skill.name: A skill
skill.where: A skill of the repository, read by the agent inside this one step.
skill.why: The step needs interpretation, lives a few hours at most and may start again: an agent guided by a skill does it, and nothing has to hold it between two jobs.

dated_skill.name: A skill with its date
dated_skill.says: a skill is enough, with its date
dated_skill.where: A skill of the repository, with the model and the date written beside it.
dated_skill.why: The step is here because today's model is weak: keep it in the cheapest layer, test it again at each model release, and delete it when it changes nothing.

ticket_state.name: A state on the ticket
ticket_state.where: A state on the ticket or the pull request; the next event starts a short job.
ticket_state.why: Nothing runs while a person works or while the run waits: the ticket holds the state for hours or days at no cost, and each step after it is safe to do again.

human_gate.name: A human gate
human_gate.where: A state of the ticket or the pull request that only a human account may set.
human_gate.why: A person decides on something they can read and refuse: the forge records who approved, and no program can set the state in their place.

no_gate.name: No gate
no_gate.where: Nowhere: remove the gate, or give its judge something they can read and refuse.
no_gate.why: The person could not tell a good result from a bad one: an approval they cannot judge protects nothing and only adds a wait.

reusable_workflow.name: A shared CI workflow
reusable_workflow.says: this is a shared CI workflow
reusable_workflow.where: A versioned plugin and a reusable CI workflow, with a named owner.
reusable_workflow.why: Several repositories need the same step: one versioned copy with an owner stays the same everywhere, where copies drift apart.

campaign.name: A fan-out by script
campaign.says: this is a fan-out by script
campaign.where: A script that fans out, for example a CI matrix, with one writer per unit.
campaign.why: The work splits into many independent units: a script starts one writer for each and counts the results. Never a swarm of agents that share the work.

durable_engine.name: A workflow engine
durable_engine.where: A workflow engine that holds the step, outside this repository's CI.
durable_engine.why: The step lives for days inside one computation, must not run twice, or must be replayable step by step: a CI job and a ticket state cannot promise that.
